shots.phrase: Begin by framing Foundations of AI System Architecture as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results.
Consider this worked case: A learner maps the inputs, constraints, and observable result for Foundations of AI System Architecture, then checks each step against the stated claim.
Annotate each node with a brief label and connect them with arrows to show sequential flow.
Now define Image Representation in Computer Vision precisely enough that another learner could test the definition.
Consider this worked case: A 100x100 color image is stored as a 30000-element array where each triplet corresponds to red, green, and blue pixel values.
Highlight one pixel and show its RGB values as a numeric triplet.
With the foundation in place, examine how Color Conversion and Filtering operates in a concrete sequence.
Consider this worked case: Converting an RGB image to grayscale reduces three channels to one, simplifying edge detection.
Use arrows to indicate the color conversion and filtering steps.
Next, compare the choices involved in Feature Detection and Calibration and make the decision criteria explicit.
Consider this worked case: SIFT features identify keypoints like corners and edges.
Overlay a calibration grid showing how real-world distances map to image coordinates.
Apply Geometric Transforms and Segmentation to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition.
Foreground segmentation isolates moving objects from a static background.
Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step.
Examine the tradeoffs in Motion Estimation and Object Recognition, including what improves and what becomes more difficult.
Consider this worked case: Optical flow tracks pixel movement between video frames.
Annotate detected faces with bounding boxes and labels.
Stress-test the reasoning around Scene Understanding and Context with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome.
Consider this worked case: A kitchen scene is understood by recognizing a stove, a pot, and a person standing near the stove, establishing spatial and functional relationships.
Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds.
Use Evaluation and Robustness Testing to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action.
Consider this worked case: An AI model is tested with images taken at different angles, under bright and dim light, with partial occlusions, and from different camera types.
Annotate each with the tested condition.
Connect Practical Analysis Checklist to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system.
Consider this worked case: A learner maps the inputs, constraints, and observable result for Practical Analysis Checklist, then checks each step against the stated claim.
Check off each item as it relates to the pipeline components and evaluation criteria.
Finish with CSCI-331: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence - Course Foundations Companion as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis.
